smell_elimination.justification: This refactoring completely fails to eliminate the smell. Instead of extracting the inlined solver implementations back into separate methods, it extracts helper methods that perform auxiliary computations (_compute_class_statistics, _compute_within_class_scatter, etc.). The core problem—200+ lines of solver logic inline in fit()—remains completely unaddressed. The diff shows only additions of new methods but no modifications to the actual fit() method structure.

cross_file_coordination.justification: The refactoring adds new methods to the class but doesn't address any of the cross-file smell artifacts. The private helpers (_fast_mle_covariance, _direct_shrinkage, _ledoit_wolf_rescaled) are still imported and used extensively in the new methods. The private imports from sklearn.covariance remain in place. No cleanup of smell-related artifacts was attempted.

structural_soundness.justification: The new methods have poorly defined responsibilities and contain massive duplication. _compute_within_class_scatter and _compute_with_class_scatter_eigen are nearly identical (both compute within-class scatter with the same dispatch logic, just with different variable names). This creates new structural problems rather than fixing the existing ones. The methods don't represent meaningful abstractions—they're arbitrary fragments that still contain deeply nested conditionals.

code_quality.justification: The extracted methods have poor names (_compute_with_class_scatter_eigen vs _compute_within_class_scatter), inconsistent naming conventions, and contain 50-80 lines of dense, duplicated conditional logic. The duplication of the entire covariance estimation dispatch block in two separate methods is a significant code quality issue. Variable names like 'Xg_e', 'cls_cov_e', 'eff_shrink' are cryptic and inconsistent.

fragment_identification.justification: The refactoring fundamentally misidentifies what needs to be extracted. The fragments that should be extracted are the three complete solver implementations (svd, lsqr, eigen logic). Instead, it extracts auxiliary computations (class statistics, scatter matrices). The actual inlined solver code—the core of the smell—is not identified or addressed.

extraction_quality.justification: The extraction is at the wrong abstraction level and creates new problems. Instead of extracting solvers, it extracts sub-computations that are themselves duplicated (_compute_within_class_scatter and _compute_with_class_scatter_eigen are near-duplicates). The extracted methods are still 50-80 lines with complex nested conditionals, perpetuating the depth-3 inlining problem. The covariance dispatch logic remains inlined within these helper methods.

method_extraction_and_delegation_restora.justification: Complete failure on the primary objective. The diff shows no changes to the fit() method itself—only additions of new helper methods. The three solver implementations (svd, lsqr, eigen) remain 100% inline in fit(). There is no delegation structure introduced. The fit() method is unchanged in structure and still contains all 200+ lines of inline solver logic. This is the core of the smell and it's completely unaddressed.

covariance_estimation_deduplication.justification: The refactoring makes the duplication problem worse rather than better. The covariance estimation dispatch logic (the complex if/isinstance conditionals) appears at least 3 times in the new methods: once in _compute_within_class_scatter, a nearly identical copy in _compute_with_class_scatter_eigen, and once in _compute_total_scatter. No shared helper was created. The private helpers (_fast_mle_covariance, _direct_shrinkage, _ledoit_wolf_rescaled) are still used throughout. The smell's depth-3 inlining is preserved and duplicated.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring fundamentally misunderstands the problem. It attempts to extract auxiliary computations rather than the inlined solver implementations that are the core of the smell. The fit() method remains unchanged with 200+ lines of inline code, and the extracted helpers introduce new duplication (nearly identical covariance dispatch logic in 3 separate methods). The private helper imports remain, no deduplication was achieved, and the deeply_inlined_method smell persists entirely unchanged.
